newsitem.title: USA: Tyco to buy ADT for $5.4 billion, topping Western's bid.
newsitem.headline: Tyco to buy ADT for $5.4 billion, topping Western's bid.

text.p: Tyco International Ltd., seeking to strengthen its position as the world's largest provider of fire and safety systems, said Monday it agreed to buy ADT Ltd. for about $5.4 billion, topping a hostile takeover offer by Western Resources Inc.

Tyco, a diversified maker of industrial and commercial products, said under terms of the deal Tyco stockholders will receive one share in the new company for each Tyco share and ADT holders will receive 0.48133 share for each ADT share.
Based on Tyco's trading price of $57.875 Monday -- down $2.375 from Friday -- ADT shareholders will get about $27.85 for each share they own, or about $5.38 billion in stock.
Shares of ADT, a leading installer and servicer of electronic security systems, jumped $3.875 to $25.625 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
In December, ADT rejected an unsolicited cash-and-stock offer from Western Resources, valued at about $3.5 billion, saying it was inadequate and would not result in a strong strategic combination.
Tyco, based in Exeter, N.H., said Tyco shareholders would own about 64 percent of the new company and ADT shareholders the rest.
L. Dennis Kozlowski will remain chairman and chief executive of Tyco, which is expected to have annual revenues in excess of $8.5 billion after the merger, the company said.
"Tyco's acquisition of ADT is a continuation of our strategy to expand our position in service businesses through internal growth and complementary acquisitions," Kozlowski said in a statement.
Kozlowski also said that Tyco will take a $600 million charge, $250 million of it in cash, related to the transaction.

He told a conference call with investors, analysts and reporters that he expected the combination to add between $50 million and $52 million to Tyco's expected earnings in its next fiscal year, which begins July 1.
He also said that his company had not been in contact with Western Resources, a Kansas utility that owns 27 percent of ADT.

"They (Western) own about 27 percent of the (ADT) stock, so another 22 percent of the (ADT) shareholders could vote against the (Tyco) deal and it would still go forward," Kozlowski said in response to a question about Western.
Officials at Western Resources, based in Topeka, Kan., were not immediately available to comment.
Kozlowski said his company's agreement with ADT included a provision for a $150 million fee to be paid by one company to the other in the event that one abandons the pact.

ADT, based in Boca Raton, Fla., is the largest provider of electronic security services in North America and Britain, with more than 1.8 million industrial, commercial and residential customers. It had revenues of $1.7 billion last year.
The merger will combine ADT's 230 offices in 10 countries with Tyco's Fire and Safety Services group's 300 offices in more than 50 countries.
"ADT's commercial and industrial businesses are an excellent fit with Tyco's Fire and Safety Services group," ADT Chairman Michael Ashcroft said.
"This merger will enhance ADT's ability to continue its growth, not only in North America and the United Kingdom, but in all parts of the world utilizing Tyco's established infrastructure."
Ashcroft will have no active management role at the merged company but will be a member of the board.
Western resources stock rose 87.5 cents to $31 in late NYSE trading.
